name: Nylon Foundation Garments
summary: The structured underwear of the New Look years: circle-stitched cups, a waist cincher, an elastic girdle and a suspender belt. They were knitted or woven in nylon, satin and rubber-core elastic.

philosophy.core_thesis: The post-war dress needs a built body under it, and nylon and elastic make that build light, washable and soft to wear.
design_principles: Cut each cup as a cone, and stitch it in circles from the tip, so that the point holds its shape.
Narrow the waist by 5 to 8 cm with a waist cincher or a long-line bra with boning.
Knit the body in nylon tricot, so that it dries fast after washing.
Set a panel of elastic in the girdle, and fit four suspenders to the lower edge.
Fasten the bra with three hooks at the back and the girdle with a side zip.
Trim the cups with a nylon lace and a small satin bow.
Match the foundation to the dress: a strapless basque for a full skirt, a girdle for a narrow skirt.
anti_patterns: A soft, unlined cup of the 1920s bandeau
A heavy steel-busk corset of coutil
Stretch panels of elastane and powernet

silhouette.shape: A pointed, lifted bust, a very small waist and a smooth, firm hip: an hourglass built under the dress.
silhouette.line: A high bust point, a long waist line and a smooth hip line down to the thigh.
silhouette.fit: Close and firm; the stitched cup holds the bust and the girdle holds the hip and the stomach.
silhouette.proportion: Waist 5 to 8 cm below the natural waist; cup point 3 to 5 cm out from the body; girdle length 35 to 45 cm.
rules: Stitch each cup in circles from the tip to the edge.
Run the waist cincher from the bust to the hip, with boning at the sides.
Set an elastic panel at the front and the back of the girdle.
Hang four suspenders from the lower edge for the nylon stockings.
Fasten the back with hooks and eyes in three rows.

fabrics.rule: Knit the body in nylon, use satin for show, and put rubber-core elastic where the body needs to stretch.

methods: hook and eye closure in three rows
construction.closures: Three rows of hooks and eyes at the back of the bra; a side zip or a hook strip on the girdle.
construction.details: A lace edge on the cup, a satin bow at the centre, and a metal slide at the strap. A small label with the size sits at the back.

surface.pattern: Plain white, black and pink; for show, a lace overlay or a small embroidered flower.
surface.gloss: Nylon tricot at 6–15 GU; satin at 30–60 GU.
surface.wear: Nylon yellows and the elastic loses its grip after about a year of daily wear and wash.

palette.strategy: White, black and flesh pink under the dress; a bright colour or print only for the gown that shows.

processes: nylon tricot knitted on a warp machine
cups cut and stitched in circles
elastic panels sewn on a machine
boning cased by hand or machine
hooks and zips fitted in a factory
making.scale: Made in a factory in many cup and band sizes by firms in the United States; couture houses added their own foundations to the dress.
making.signs: Circle stitches on the cup, an elastic panel, four suspenders, hooks in rows, and a size label.

pieces.form: Circle-stitched conical cups in nylon tricot with a lace edge
Strapless long-line basque with spring-steel boning, in satin
Roll-on girdle with an elastic panel and four suspenders
Wide belt of satin with four clips for the stockings
Full-fashioned nylon stockings with a back seam
Layered petticoat of nylon net under a full skirt

canonical_works.work: Nylon stockings shown at the New York World's Fair
Long cotton corset with elastic side panels

evidence.title: Stretch nylon girdle with a lace panel, 1960s

emotion.target_response: A sense of polish and control: a smooth line, a lifted bust and a body that fills the post-war dress.

use_cases: a museum label or object study
a history of the girdle and the bra
avoid_when: the brief wants a soft 1960s bra with no seam
the brief wants a boned coutil corset

modifiers.how: Remove the stitched cone and the boning, and use a sheer, soft tricot cup with no seam.
Match the cincher and the cup point to the small waist and the full skirt of the dress.

ornament_level.note: Day foundations are plain; evening basques carry lace and satin.
